title: WakeMark for Raycast
description: Search synced X bookmarks and Ask AI from Raycast. History import stays in the Chrome extension.

hero.title: WakeMark in your launcher
hero.subtitle: Search your library and ask questions from Raycast. Sign in through wakemark.app — the same account as the website and Chrome extension.

overview.title: What it does
overview.p1: The Raycast extension is a companion, not a Chrome replacement. It talks to the same WakeMark APIs the Chrome popup uses for search and Ask AI.

points.search: Search Bookmarks: type a keyword, handle, or phrase and open the original post.
points.ask: Ask AI: questions are answered from your synced bookmarks, with links you can copy.
points.auth: Sign in through wakemark.app. Chrome and Raycast keep separate device keys, so both can stay connected.
points.scope: It only sees bookmarks already in WakeMark. Import years of X history with the Chrome extension.

install.title: Install
install.step1Body: Search for WakeMark in the Raycast Store, or import the local raycast/ folder while developing.
install.step2Body: Run Sign In (or Search Bookmarks while signed out). Raycast opens wakemark.app; after you approve, return to Raycast.
install.step3Body: Search and Ask AI use bookmarks already in WakeMark. Connect X and finish a sync in the dashboard if the list is empty.

notIncluded.title: What stays in Chrome
notIncluded.p1: Raycast cannot inject into x.com, so it cannot scroll your bookmark timeline or intercept GraphQL the way the Chrome extension does.

items.sidebar: A side panel next to the page you are reading
items.sitePing: The website’s one-click “import history” button, which talks to Chrome only

faq.title: Troubleshooting
faq.q1: Sign in opened a tab but Raycast still looks signed out
faq.a1: Finish signing in on wakemark.app and wait until the page says connected. The command polls for about two minutes. Run Sign In again if it timed out.
faq.a2: Raycast only searches bookmarks already synced to WakeMark. Open the dashboard, connect X if needed, then try again.
faq.q3: I use both Chrome and Raycast
faq.a3: That is expected. Sign in once in each; they do not share storage. History import still happens in Chrome.
